City council bans delivery robots from sidewalks after complaints

The city council voted four to one on Tuesday evening to bar sidewalk delivery robots from the downtown core for twelve months, after residents complained that the machines were blocking wheelchair users near the transit station on Main Street.

Operators of the two companies affected said they would comply immediately but warned that the ban would push last-mile deliveries back into vans, which studies suggest are far more likely to cause injuries per package delivered.

A council member said the ordinance would be revisited in the autumn with input from disability advocates, delivery firms and the transit authority before any permanent rule is written.
